Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:

If we add the real number [MATH: \color{blue}2] and the imaginary number [MATH: {\color{red}3\textrm{i}},] we get the complex number [MATH: {\color{blue}2} +{\color{red}3\textrm{i}}.]

Content:
This complex number has real part equal to [MATH: \color{blue}2] and imaginary part equal to [MATH: {\color{red}3},] which we write as

Content:
[MATH: Re(2 + 3\textrm{i})|= 2,; Im(2 + 3\textrm{i})|= 3.]

Content:
In general, we write a complex number as [MATH: {\color{blue}a} + {\color{red}b\textrm{i}},] where [MATH: \color{blue}a] is the real part and [MATH: \color{red}b] is the imaginary part.
